must_read.title: Periodontitis-Associated Shifts in Bloodstream Infections among Allo-HSCT Recipients
must_read.abstract: This study aimed to investigate how periodontitis would alter bloodstream infections (BSIs) in patients undergoing allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (allo-HSCT). We hypothesized that periodontitis would alter the microbiological profile of BSIs, particularly the relative prevalence of viridans group streptococci (VGS), common oral bacteria frequently implicated in BSIs in allo-HSCT recipients, and other non-VGS organisms. We further investigated whether these microbiological changes were associated with clinical outcomes and alterations in VGS-specific humoral immune responses. A retrospective cohort (n = 489 patients, 2010-2020) and a prospective cohort (n = 149 patients, 2021-2022) were included for this observational study recruited from Princess Margaret Cancer Centre. Patients were categorized based on pretransplant history of periodontitis. BSIs occurring during the hospitalization period and mortality up to 1,000 days posttransplant were compared between patients with and without periodontitis. Pretransplant serum samples from the prospective cohort were analyzed for VGS-specific IgG and IgA using flow cytometry. There was no difference in the rates of BSI between groups; however, in the retrospective cohort, patients with a history of periodontitis had a higher incidence of non-VGS BSIs (76.7% vs. 56.8%, P = 0.019). A similar, though nonsignificant, trend was observed in the prospective cohort (63.4% vs. 45.8%, P = 0.16). Notably, the shift toward non-VGS BSIs was stage-dependent, increasing with advanced periodontitis in both cohorts (P = 0.009 and P = 0.025, respectively). Patients with periodontitis had almost double the risk of mortality compared to those without (retrospective: hazard ratio [HR] = 1.86; 95% confidence interval [CI] = 1.31-2.69; P < 0.001; prospective: HR = 1.82; 95% CI = 0.98-3.57; P = 0.06). Elevated VGS-specific IgG and IgA levels were observed in patients with periodontitis, with lower IgG levels correlating with VGS BSIs. History of periodontitis was associated with differences in BSI microbiology, including a higher proportion of non-VGS BSIs among patients who developed BSIs, and with poorer survival outcomes in allo-HSCT recipients.

scan.title: Long-Term Structural Stability and Maturation of Centimeter-Scale Stretch-Grown Sensory Axons Following Collagen Encapsulation

scan.abstract: Peripheral nerve injury (PNI) remains a significant clinical challenge due to limited biologically active regeneration strategies. Tissue engineered nerve grafts (TENGs) comprising long-projecting, stretch-grown axon tracts have emerged as a promising strategy to guide regeneration by creating a living bridge guiding and aiding native regeneration processes. However, their long-term structural stability remains incompletely understood. In this study, we evaluated the effects of dorsal root ganglia (DRG) plating density on the structural stability and morphology of mechanically stretch-grown TENGs over 5-7 weeks after three-dimensional collagen-encapsulation and removal from the mechanobioreactor. TENGs generated from 20, 40, or 80 DRG maintained neuronal-axonal phenotype and exhibited robust longitudinal axonal alignment across all conditions. While higher-density TENGs demonstrated a modest but significant reduction in length over time, overall contraction remained limited, and contraction rates were not significantly different among the groups. Stretch-grown axons maintained over 90% of their immediate post-stretch length out to 5-7 weeks post-encapsulation. Higher density TENGs also exhibited increased integration and fusion of DRG, forming continuous neuronal somatic fields and the ends of the TENGs and running perpendicular to the stretch-grown axons. Moreover, quantitative analyses revealed density- and time-dependent remodeling of axonal fascicular architecture, characterized by increased fascicle diameter without substantial changes in fascicle number, consistent with progressive axonal thickening, bundling and network consolidation. Despite this maturation-associated remodeling, TENGs preserved overall structural integrity and alignment through 7 weeks in culture. Collectively, these findings establish TENGs as mechanically stable, dynamically remodeling tissues and support their potential use as nerve repair strategies requiring graft stability over clinically relevant timeframes. scan.title: Fifteen Years of the PUFA Index in Oral Epidemiology: A Systematic Review of Global Application and Reporting
scan.abstract: OBJECTIVES: The PUFA index records the presence of pulpal involvement, ulceration, fistula, and abscess to quantify the clinical consequences of untreated dental caries. The PUFA index captures the prevalence and severity of oral conditions, making it useful for surveillance, research, and advocacy. After 15 years of global use, this systematic review synthesises how the PUFA index has been applied and reported. METHODS: Following PRISMA 2020 guidelines, seven databases were searched: PubMed, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science, CINAHL, Global Health, and Google Scholar. Eligible studies were published between 2010 and 2025 and reported original epidemiological data using the PUFA index. Data extraction captured study design, population, dentition type, PUFA reporting formats, examiner details, and use of complementary indices. Descriptive synthesis was performed with high inter-rater reliability among reviewers (96.5%). RESULTS: Out of 4438 records, 260 studies from 53 countries met the inclusion criteria. PUFA was predominantly applied in low- and middle-income countries across the life course, but with a focus on children and adolescents. Nearly half of the studies (48.8%) examined associations between PUFA and health outcomes, and over one-third (37.7%) applied PUFA in population surveillance. Reporting practices varied, and examiner type was specified in about half of the studies (47.3%), with dentists being the most common (82.9%). While methodological rigour was generally good, there were inconsistencies in reporting formats and limited availability of inter- and intra-examiner reliability data. CONCLUSIONS: The PUFA index is a recognized oral health index that has shown steady adoption across numerous studies and diverse populations. Its global credibility has positioned it for integration into modern surveillance frameworks, including the updated WHO STEPS Oral Health Module. Future priorities include standardizing reporting, strengthening integration into surveillance systems, and exploring how the PUFA index can be used in program evaluation to better inform policy and reduce oral health inequities.

scan.title: Probe Accuracy and Agreement and Patient Preferences in Peri-Implant Probing Depth Assessment: A Cross-Sectional Study

scan.cluster: 种植体周的免疫微环境（巨…
scan.abstract: OBJECTIVES: To record the accuracy and agreement of three types of probes (i.e., a common metal probe and two types of flexible probes) for peri-implant probing depth (PD) assessment, including patient-reported outcomes (PRO). METHODS: Fifty patients (85 implants) with an implant-supported restoration were included. Peri-implant PD was recorded with a metal, plastic, and electronic probe. Pain/discomfort and patient preference were registered. After removing the prosthetic restoration, the correct peri-implant PD (cPD), the mucosal height (MH), and the PD measured from the implant level (iPD) were assessed. RESULTS: Good accuracy and agreement were noted for PD measurements with the metal and plastic probe. They differed in approximately 80% of the measurements by < 1.5 mm from cPD, and on average, an underestimation of 0.5 mm occurred. The accuracy of the metal probe was negatively influenced by a thick peri-implant mucosal phenotype. A direct comparison of the metal and plastic probes showed perfect agreement in 68.7% of the cases. Patients reported significantly less pain/discomfort when the plastic probe was used compared to the metal probe. The electronic probe was unreliable and differed by ≥ 1.5 mm from cPD in 65% of the measurements. CONCLUSIONS: While the electronic probe was unreliable, the metal and plastic probes were relatively accurate and comparable for assessing peri-implant PD; the plastic probe caused less pain/discomfort. However, in approximately 1/5 of the measurements a ≥ 1.5 mm deviation from the correct value (cPD) may occur, and the accuracy of the metal probe appears negatively influenced by a thick peri-implant mucosal phenotype. TRIAL REGISTRATION: The protocol was registered at clinicaltrials.gov (NCT05332327).
